report:
## Conclusion

Your assessment is largely correct: the best available evidence does **not** support ginkgo extract as an effective treatment for tinnitus symptoms.

### Evidence Summary

**Cochrane systematic review** (the gold standard for evidence synthesis), covering four trials with 1,543 participants, concluded there is **no reliable evidence** that ginkgo biloba reduces tinnitus severity compared to placebo ([Cochrane](https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD003852_ginkgo-biloba-tinnitus); [Ear Labs summary](https://earlabs.app/articles/ginkgo-biloba-tinnitus-evidence/)).

A **double-blind, placebo-controlled trial** found that ginkgo extract LI 1370 had "no greater therapeutic effect than placebo in treating tinnitus" ([PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC26593/)).

A **randomized controlled trial** on EGb 761 noted that "evidence supporting its efficacy remains limited" ([Tinnitus Journal](https://www.tinnitusjournal.com/articles/the-effectiveness-of-ginkgo-biloba-extract-egb-761-in-tinnitus-a-randomizedcontrolled-trial.pdf)).

### Nuance

One systematic review argued that the *standardized* extract EGb 761® showed efficacy in three trials and called it "an evidence-based treatment option" ([Taylor & Francis](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.2147/NDT.S22793)). However, this contrasts with the Cochrane review's broader and more rigorous assessment. Results across trials have been inconsistent, partly due to differences in extract type, dosage, and outcome measures ([PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3157487/)).

### Bottom Line

The weight of high-quality evidence—particularly the Cochrane review—indicates ginkgo extract does **not** reliably relieve tinnitus symptoms beyond placebo. While some individual studies of specific standardized extracts suggest modest benefit, the overall evidence is insufficient to recommend ginkgo for tinnitus.
